title: Who's Who: Matteo Orsini
summary: Resonance investigator whose work remains part of the record of modern Eidetics.
author: Who's Who Desk
paragraphs: The Correspondent adds Matteo Orsini (1804–1868) to its Who's Who of Eideticians, recording a resonance investigator whose name still attends serious discussion of the Eidetic Stratum.

Orsini’s long series of measurements helped establish sonance in 1837 as patterned variation between an object and its Referent. He borrowed the language of musical intervals while warning that sonance was neither sound nor a tune.
His notebooks contain several unexplained signals whose intervals recur in modern receiving halls.

For Alderwick readers, Matteo Orsini is remembered not as an ornament to legend but as a figure whose work helps explain why Eideticians prize careful terms, repeatable evidence and a sober account of what remains unknown.
